source: Marini JJ, Rodriguez RM, Lamb VJ. The inspiratory work of breathing during assist-control ventilation. Am Rev Respir Dis 1986; 134(5):902-909; MacIntyre NR. Patient-ventilator interactions: optimizing conventional modes of mechanical ventilation. Respir Care 2011; 56(1):43-57.
claim: In volume control with fixed constant flow set well below patient inspiratory demand (inspFlowLpm 25 L/min square vs patient demand flow > 60 L/min, Pmus 18 cmH2O), vigorous patient effort distorts airway pressure below the passive trajectory, generating a scooped concave pressure waveform and flow starvation dyssynchrony.
